title: Idea 1 • Question 1
prompt: If the sequence A, −3, 9, B, … is a geometric sequence, find the common ratio (r) and the values of A and B.
hint: Divide 9 by −3 to find the common ratio r, then work backward for A and forward for B.

title: Idea 1 • Question 2
prompt: If the sequence A, 1/3, 1/9, B, … is a geometric sequence, find the common ratio (r) and the values of A and B.

title: Idea 1 • Question 3
prompt: If the sequence A, −1/4, 1/8, B, … is a geometric sequence, find the common ratio (r) and the values of A and B.
hint: Divide (1/8) by (−1/4) to find r, watching the signs carefully.

title: Idea 2 • Question 4
prompt: In an increasing geometric sequence, if a₁ + a₃ = 17 and a₂ = 4, then find a₅.
hint: Express a₁ = a₂/r and a₃ = a₂·r, then solve 4/r + 4r = 17 for r > 1.
explanation: 4/r + 4r = 17 gives 4r² − 17r + 4 = 0, so r = 4 (increasing) and a₁ = 1. Thus a₅ = 1 · 4⁴ = 256.

title: Idea 2 • Question 5
prompt: In an increasing geometric sequence, if a₁ + a₃ = 10 and a₂ = 3, then find a₅.
hint: Substitute a₁ = 3/r and a₃ = 3r into a₁ + a₃ = 10, picking r > 1.
explanation: 3/r + 3r = 10 gives 3r² − 10r + 3 = 0, so r = 3 (increasing) and a₁ = 1. Thus a₅ = 1 · 3⁴ = 81.

title: Idea 2 • Question 6
prompt: In an increasing geometric sequence, if a₁ + a₃ = 26 and a₂ = 5, then find a₄.
hint: Solve 5/r + 5r = 26 for r > 1, then compute a₄ = a₁ · r³.
explanation: 5/r + 5r = 26 gives 5r² − 26r + 5 = 0, so r = 5 (increasing) and a₁ = 1. Thus a₄ = 1 · 5³ = 125.

title: Idea 3 • Question 7
prompt: When the 3 numbers a, b, 2 form an arithmetic sequence in this order, and a, 2, b form a geometric sequence in this order, find the values of a and b.
hint: Use 2b = a + 2 for the arithmetic sequence and ab = 2² = 4 for the geometric sequence.
explanation: From a = 2b − 2 and ab = 4, we get (2b − 2)b = 4 → b² − b − 2 = 0, so b = 2 (a = 2) or b = −1 (a = −4).

title: Idea 3 • Question 8
prompt: When the 3 numbers a, b, 6 form an arithmetic sequence in this order, and a, 6, b form a geometric sequence in this order, find the values of a and b.
explanation: From a = 2b − 6 and ab = 36, we get b² − 3b − 18 = 0, so b = 6 (a = 6) or b = −3 (a = −12).

title: Idea 3 • Question 9
prompt: When the 3 numbers a, b, 8 form an arithmetic sequence in this order, and a, 8, b form a geometric sequence in this order, find the values of a and b.
explanation: From a = 2b − 8 and ab = 64, we get b² − 4b − 32 = 0, so b = 8 (a = 8) or b = −4 (a = −16).

title: Idea 4 • Question 10
prompt: Find the sum (Sₙ) from the first term to the n-th term of the following geometric sequence: 4, −12, 36, −108, …
hint: Use Sₙ = a(1 − r^n) / (1 − r) with a = 4 and r = −3.

title: Idea 5 • Question 13

hint: Since ar = 8, write a = 8/r and solve 8/r + 8 + 8r = 42.
